salarySources.claim: Waiter adverts in 2026 mostly pay N50,000 to N120,000 a month, most common N70,000; Lagos casual dining N70,000 to N120,000.
Lagos restaurant cashier advert (2026) at N70,000 a month.
Single-site restaurant managers in Lagos commonly earn N150,000 to N250,000 a month; upscale N250,000 to N400,000.
Regional/area manager gross pay mostly N201,991 to N841,715 a month, about N545,800 after 5 years (small sample).
Labourer survey range N142,487 to N265,048 gross a month (small sample, formal employers; game figure set near the N70,000 minimum wage typical of farm and informal work).
Warehouseman survey range N137,467 to N326,282 gross a month (small sample; game loader figure set lower for an unskilled loader).
Cooks typically earn N23,436 to N58,127 a month nationally (low-end survey; game figure raised above the N70,000 minimum wage for Lagos).

tax.realRule: Nigeria Tax Act 2025 (from 1 Jan 2026): companies with turnover up to N100m a year and fixed assets up to N250m pay no company income tax, capital gains tax or development levy. Larger companies pay 30% company income tax plus a 4% development levy on assessable profits. VAT stays 7.5%.
tax.label: Company tax + levy

sources.claim: Small company = turnover of N100m or below and fixed assets not above N250m; exempt from CIT, CGT and the 4% development levy; VAT retained at 7.5%.
Companies above N100m turnover keep paying 30% corporate tax plus a new 4% development levy; effective 1 January 2026.
The 4% development levy replaces the tertiary education tax, NITDA, NASENI and police trust fund levies.

notes: Sim (econ_sim.py): cash 0 at day 30, payroll 15% of revenue daily, 10% tax on profit every 30 days with NO exemption applied, greedy cheapest-first. Next regional manager unlocks only when the current region is full. p<1 is deliberate: flatter costs keep waits at 1-3 days. 94% of waits are 3 days or less.
